title: Commonwealth Games: Jadumani wins high-octane India-Pakistan bout, Preeti one win away from medal
summary: India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman 5-0 at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, dedicating his win to Kargil heroes. Preeti Pawar advanced via RSC and is one win away from a Commonwealth Games medal. Aditya Pratap lost his 65kg opener to Uganda's Nuhu Batte 2:3.
content:
Published- July 27, 2026 02:20 am IST - Glasgow

India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam outclassed Pakistan's Sumama Rehman in a high-voltage contest as Asian Games bronze medallist Preeti Pawar also advanced into the quarterfinals of the Commonwealth Games boxing competition in Glasgow on Sunday (July 26, 2026).

Amid thunderous chants of "Bharat Mata ki Jai" and "India, India" ringing around the SEC Centre, the atmosphere crackled with emotion long before the opening bell of Jadumani's bout.

The Army boxer responded in style, registering a unanimous 5-0 victory through superior technique, speed and ringcraft.

Jadumani, who had dedicated his victory to the heroes of the Kargil War on Kargil Vijay Diwas, reiterated his ambition after another commanding performance. "I want to dedicate this win to Kargil heroes. I want to defeat everyone and get gold for India," he said.

After a watchful opening round, Jadumani quickly figured out his opponent's rhythm and took complete control of the contest. He repeatedly found the target with sharp hooks and straight punches, forcing the referee to give a standing count to Rehman in the second round after a stinging right hand.

With the outcome virtually decided, Jadumani began the final round confidently, standing his ground in the centre of the ring and even inviting Rehman to attack before countering with superior speed and movement. The unanimous decision reflected his dominance across tactics and tempo.

Preeti (54kg) was similarly convincing, winning her pre-quarterfinal contest against Deborah Mtenje of Malawi via Referee Stop Contest (RSC) in the second round. The Malawi boxer faced two standing counts, one in each round, and the referee halted the bout with 47 seconds left in the second round. Preeti also earned the unanimous nod of all five judges in the first round.

The win puts Preeti one victory away from securing her maiden Commonwealth Games medal; she arrives in Glasgow with a 2022 Asian Games bronze and a 2025 New Delhi World Cup gold to her name.

The third Indian boxer in action, Aditya Pratap, was less fortunate, losing his opening 65kg bout to Uganda's Nuhu Batte by a 2-3 decision.
